sample_unit: prospectively collected sonographic gallbladder videos (from 207 infants) read by 18 radiologists
models_evaluated: Interpretable deep learning smartphone app model for biliary atresia (redeveloped)

links.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic AUC with versus without AI assistance in real-world mimic settings
links.effect: AI assistance raised average AUC from 0.773 to 0.835 for junior radiologists and from 0.749 to 0.805 for senior radiologists.
links.quote: Furthermore, the new model could aid both junior and senior radiologists to improve their diagnostic performances, with the average AUC increasing from 0.773 to 0.835 for junior radiologists and from 0.749 to 0.805 for senior radiologists.

links.outcome: AI model diagnostic AUC compared with radiologists and previous model on same data
links.effect: New model AUC 0.860 vs experienced radiologists 0.876, junior 0.773, senior 0.749; outperformed prior model on external set (AUC 0.924 vs 0.908, P = 0.004).
links.quote: When tested in real-world mimic settings using 333 sonographic gallbladder videos, the new model performed comparable to experienced pediatric radiologists (average AUC 0.860 vs 0.876) and outperformed junior radiologists (average AUC 0.838 vs 0.773) and senior radiologists (average AUC 0.829 vs 0.749).

unlisted_practices: Retraining the model on smartphone photos derived from original images to enable practical smartphone-based deployment

screen.reason: Empirical multireader study evaluating whether using an AI-based smartphone app improves the diagnostic performance of junior and senior radiologists compared to unassisted reading in simulated real-world settings.

primary.practice: AI-assisted clinician reading vs unassisted reading
